top_story.headline: Prison bureau signed four contracts with GEO Reentry in the weeks before Pamela Bondi's successor was confirmed; the company gave $4.4 million to MAGA Inc.
top_story.dek: Federal Election Commission records tie the company to large giving to a Trump-world committee.
paragraphs: The Federal Prison System (Bureau of Prisons) awarded four residential reentry and home-confinement contracts, worth about $7.4 million combined, to Geo Reentry Inc between July 22 and August 7, 2026. Todd Blanche was confirmed as the successor to Pamela Bondi at the Department of Justice on August 8, 2026.

The largest is $2,671,092 for a Bronx, New York center, signed August 7, one day before the confirmation. The others are $2,178,408 (Las Vegas, signed August 6), $1,488,823 (Kansas City, Kansas area, option year seven, signed July 22) and $1,070,863 (Brownsville, Texas, option year two, signed July 22).

Federal Election Commission records show the company itself gave $4,413,000 to MAGA Inc. That shows the company's giving, not who owns it. Two of the four awards are option-year exercises on existing contracts.

sections.headline: Geo Reentry Inc won $2,671,092 from Federal Prison System / Bureau of Prisons as Pamela Bondi was leaving — FEC links it to donors to Trump-world committees
paragraphs: 4 award(s) went to vendors tied by FEC records to the agency head's own donors or to large Trump-world giving, around a change at the top of the agency.

Pekoske, Erika L. McEntarfer, Roselyn Tso, Pamela Bondi, Susan Monarez, Tulsi Gabbard): $1 million+ awards in the 30 days before each successor's confirmation, plus new $2 million+ awards at those agencies. Donor data: FEC contributions (2024 and 2026 cycles) to the departing/arriving head's own committees and to Trump's committees, MAGA Inc., the Trump National Committee JFC and the Republican National Committee; matched on the vendor's exact name as donor, as donors' stated employer, or as the employer of a donor whose occupation is owner/executive.

sections.headline: No sole-source justifications posted; 152 new solicitations, nearly all routine Defense Logistics Agency buys
paragraphs: No new sole-source justifications turned up in the window, and 152 new solicitations were posted. Three more notices were amendments or reposts of solicitations already listed earlier today and are not repeated.

items: Department of the Navy (Military Sealift Command) — solicitation for a mid-term availability (scheduled maintenance period) on the expeditionary fast transport USNS Point Loma (N3220526R6128).
U.S. Marine Corps — solicitation for barge transportation to Ie Shima, Japan; the description is truncated in the data (M2900027Q3000).
United States Holocaust Memorial Museum — presolicitation request for information, market research for a 2027 managed security services contract (95476727RFI-MSSP).

blocks.text: Solicitations not listed: 146 routine, including Defense Logistics Agency 142 (DLA Land and Maritime 89, DLA Aviation 32, DLA Troop Support 21), Department of Veterans Affairs 3 and Department of the Navy 1. Three flagged Defense Logistics Agency parts solicitations (actuator, motor controller, bearing seat) were already listed earlier today and are omitted.

sections.headline: No new contract awards of $100,000 or more to report
paragraphs: No new awards cleared the $2 million threshold, and none under $2 million were screened as new, so there was nothing to flag.

sections.headline: No new apportionment files were approved this week
paragraphs: The Office of Management and Budget released no new apportionment notices between September 29 and October 4. Routine spend plans were reviewed but showed no notable changes or conditioning.

footer.coverage_window: October 3-4, 2026 (Pacific time), with a trailing sweep for USAspending contract actions.
footer.sources: OMB apportionment data via openomb.org and apportionment-public.max.gov; USAspending.gov API; SAM.gov Get Opportunities Public API; Federal Election Commission contribution records.
footer.known_gaps: No tasks were skipped. All three sources were reachable with no errors. SAM.gov returned zero sole-source justifications in the window.
